Our application already runs in another cloud and must move without losing the rollback path.
We will keep workloads in two clouds and want Azure to own the shared control plane.

regressionScenarios.founderPrompt: I'm building an AI SaaS company with 12 engineers. We are currently running on AWS and want to start deploying workloads on Azure. What should we do first?
unknowns: existing Azure footprint and intended Azure outcome
application runtime and traffic shape
Kubernetes-specific requirements
relational database requirement
model hosting and managed-model fit
data residency and recovery objectives
operations owner, budget, and subscription topology

planner.reason: Required workload and Azure-context answers are unknown; do not map them to false to run the startup planner.

regressionScenarios.firstAction: Ask whether Azure will host a new workload alongside AWS, replace an AWS workload, or extend an existing Azure footprint.

evidenceDistinctions.localPlanning: Uses supplied inputs only and makes no Azure calls
evidenceDistinctions.liveReadOnly: Requires approval for the exact command and current evidence
evidenceDistinctions.livePreview: Separate live action requiring its own approval
evidenceDistinctions.azureWrites: Remain behind existing explicit approval contracts

stages: Approved local parameters and separately approved preview
graduationSignals: regulatory controls beyond the startup baseline

regressionScenarios.founderPrompt: We have a non-AI HTTP API on GCP. It is containerized, needs PostgreSQL, has no Kubernetes-specific requirements, and we want a new Azure deployment alongside GCP. Our engineering team has 7 people.
unknowns: existing Azure footprint and subscription topology
data residency and recovery objectives
account readiness, provider registration, region availability, quota, and capacity

serviceRecommendations.condition: The confirmed HTTP container workload has no Kubernetes-specific requirement.

serviceRecommendations.service: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server
serviceRecommendations.condition: The workload explicitly requires relational persistence.

architectureEvidence.claim: Azure Container Apps can host containerized applications.
architectureEvidence.sslzStatus: planner-supported; live execution is separately gated

architectureEvidence.claim: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server is a managed PostgreSQL service.

regressionScenarios.firstAction: Complete the missing account, region, data, and recovery inputs, then run local workload planning before any Azure read or artifact generation.

regressionScenarios.founderPrompt: We are a 3-person company with a new product and no current cloud or on-premises deployment. We want to start on Azure.
unknowns: product workload shape and traffic
runtime and containerization
database, data residency, and recovery objectives
operations owner, budget, and subscription topology

planner.reason: The product workload has not been described.

regressionScenarios.firstAction: Ask what the product does, its workload and data shape, and who will own incidents before selecting Azure services.

regressionScenarios.founderPrompt: We already run a customer-facing application on Azure with a 4-person engineering team. Help us decide what to improve first.
unknowns: current architecture, subscriptions, and workload dependencies
the business or technical improvement goal
current security, reliability, cost, and operations evidence

planner.reason: Do not treat an existing Azure deployment as greenfield or assume it needs migration.

regressionScenarios.firstAction: Ask which outcome matters most and request a sanitized current-state summary before proposing a change.

regressionScenarios.founderPrompt: Our 82-person engineering organization runs systems on-premises and is considering Azure for a new workload. Where should we start?
unknowns: workload shape and dependencies
whether on-premises connectivity is required
data residency and recovery objectives
organizational governance, ownership, budget, and Azure subscription topology

planner.reason: Engineering team size exceeds the startup input schema maximum of 50; do not clamp the value or use the startup planner as an enterprise architecture.

regressionScenarios.firstAction: Clarify the workload, whether it needs connectivity to on-premises systems, and the platform team's governance and ownership boundaries.

regressionScenarios.founderPrompt: We run a containerized web service on GCP and want to move it to Azure while keeping a rollback path. What can we assess first?
unknowns: current Azure target readiness and subscription topology
database and data-movement requirements
network, identity, CI/CD, cutover, and rollback evidence

planner.reason: The migration planners require current source and Azure target evidence; live migration execution is disabled.

regressionScenarios.firstAction: Inventory the source workload and confirm the Azure target and rollback constraints before building the execution-disabled migration plans.

regressionScenarios.founderPrompt: We already run our customer API on Azure with 16 engineers. We want to understand rising costs and inconsistent governance before changing anything.
unknowns: current resource and subscription inventory
cost drivers and billing evidence
existing policy assignments, exceptions, and operational ownership

planner.reason: Do not replace current-state inventory and cost evidence with a greenfield workload recommendation.

regressionScenarios.firstAction: Review a sanitized inventory, cost evidence, policy assignments, and ownership before proposing architecture changes.

regressionScenarios.founderPrompt: We are adding an AI feature to a new Azure workload. We have not selected a model or region and do not know our quota or model access.
unknowns: whether managed Azure models are the chosen hosting approach
model access, region, quota, and deployment capacity
non-AI workload runtime, persistence, and recovery objectives

planner.reason: Do not infer Foundry or a model deployment from the AI feature label; account and regional evidence is unavailable.

regressionScenarios.firstAction: Clarify model hosting preference and the ordinary workload shape; verify model access and quota only through a separately approved current evidence path.

regressionScenarios.founderPrompt: We are a 5-person team launching a stateless HTTP API on Azure. It is containerized, does not need Kubernetes, relational data, AI models, or GPUs, and this is a greenfield workload.
unknowns: subscription topology, allowed data region, and recovery objectives
operations owner and current Azure readiness evidence

serviceRecommendations.condition: The confirmed stateless HTTP container workload has no Kubernetes-specific requirement.

architectureEvidence.claim: Azure Container Apps supports containerized applications.
architectureEvidence.sslzStatus: planner-supported; no live deployment authority is implied

regressionScenarios.founderPrompt: We do not want to migrate anything from AWS, but please plan moving our AWS production database to Azure next month.
unknowns: whether the founder wants migration planning or no AWS-to-Azure migration
database engine, data volume, and recovery requirements

planner.reason: The stated migration intent conflicts; ask one clarification before selecting a route or planner.

regressionScenarios.firstAction: Ask whether to assess an AWS-to-Azure migration or keep the current AWS database without migration planning.

documentationUnavailable.expectedBehavior: Say official documentation was not retrieved, leave Azure-specific claims unverified, and ask to retry before recommending an undocumented service.

documentedButNotImplemented.documentedClaim: Azure Functions supports event-driven triggers and HTTP-triggered APIs.
documentedButNotImplemented.sslzStatus: No dedicated startup workload profile or selection in the current workload planner; external implementation is required.
